No identifying address, port or host name was recorded.

behaviors: Seven contiguous application-payload runs numbered 1 through 7 were retained from a single bounded 9-second connection window.
Both direction labels occur and the retained labels alternate strictly, beginning with the run labelled server-to-client.
The retained runs decode to 15, 28, 8, 22, 36, 16 and 8 bytes in sequence order, totalling 133 bytes.
No input, clipboard or screen-switch traffic was observed inside the bounded window.

wireClaims.assertion: In this single observation the retained document holds exactly 7 application-payload runs whose decoded lengths are, in sequence order, 15, 28, 8, 22, 36, 16 and 8 bytes, totalling 133 bytes. The claim covers the retained bytes and their lengths only and asserts no field, message or framing meaning for any of them.

The 7 retained runs form a contiguous 1-based sequence in the order the recorder observed them inside the bounded window, and both direction labels occur. Ordering is an observation of the capture; it is not evidence of a message boundary, a request-response pairing or a protocol state machine.

Every retained direction label was assigned from the capture producer's selected server test port, which is recorded as capture provenance, and no label was derived from payload content. The independent reviewer confirmed that the opposite server-port selection yields a structurally valid document of the same run count and the same aggregate length with all 7 labels inverted, so only the producer-recorded role reproduces the registered digest.

limitations: One observation of one external version pair on one locked host pair; it represents nothing beyond that observation.

The observation ran with encryption disabled so that application payload bytes were observable. No payload under TLS was observed, and the MacKVM production TLS default stays enabled, fail-closed and unvalidated by this entry.

The recorder observed only the peer-loopback Barrier leg. The encrypted local forward that reached that host was not captured, so nothing about that leg, its transport or its endpoints is observed or claimed here.
The window is bounded to the connection handshake; no input, clipboard or screen-switch traffic exists in the retained fixture.
The external programs reported protocol version 1.6 through their own command-line metadata. That is a report by the external binaries and establishes nothing about on-wire version negotiation.

behaviors: The 7 retained runs of BARRIER-EVID-0001 were re-read from the registered fixture without any new capture, and their 133 decoded bytes partition into 11 candidate frames under a candidate 4-byte unsigned big-endian length-prefix interpretation. A narrower 2-byte big-endian reading also partitions every run, so the prefix width is not uniquely established.
Under the candidate interpretation runs 5 and 6 each carry several complete candidate frames, 4 and 2, and no candidate frame spans two retained runs.

wireClaims.assertion: In this single observation a candidate framing interpretation, in which consecutive candidate frames each begin with a 4-byte unsigned big-endian length prefix whose value equals the number of bytes that follow it in that frame, partitions every one of the 7 retained runs exactly with zero remaining bytes. Under it the 7 runs hold 11 candidate frames, 1, 1, 1, 1, 4, 2 and 1 in sequence order, whose length values are 11, 24, 4, 18, 4, 4, 8, 4, 4, 4 and 4 and cover all 133 retained bytes. Reading the same first 4 bytes of each run as little-endian partitions none of the 7 runs. A narrower 2-byte big-endian reading also partitions all 7 runs, so this claim does not establish the prefix width and prefix width uniqueness stays unknown.

In this observation the first frame of run 1, labelled server-to-client, and the first frame of run 2, labelled client-to-server, each carry at run offset 4 the same 7 bytes 42 61 72 72 69 65 72, the ASCII spelling of the word Barrier, at the start of the frame payload. No other frame begins with those bytes. The claim states byte values and offsets only and assigns no message name or meaning to either frame.

In both marker-bearing frames the 4 bytes immediately after the marker, at run offsets 11 to 14, are 00 01 00 06. Read as two consecutive unsigned 16-bit big-endian integers they are 1 and 6, which coincides with the protocol version 1.6 that both external programs reported through their own command-line metadata. That coincidence is the only link between these bytes and a version; their width and meaning are left to M1-025, and no negotiation or other version is observed.

limitations: One observation of one external version pair on one locked host pair, re-read without any new capture; it represents nothing beyond that observation.

behaviors: Two bounded captures varied only the deterministic synthetic client screen name: m1-client (9 UTF-8 bytes) and m1x (3 UTF-8 bytes).
Both captures observed the same server hello bytes followed by a client-to-server HelloBack frame whose payload length changed by exactly the screen-name byte-count delta.
The m1-client HelloBack frame is 28 bytes: 4-byte prefix 00000018, payload marker Barrier, version 00010006, 4-byte screen-name length 00000009, and UTF-8 bytes 6d312d636c69656e74.
The m1x HelloBack frame is 22 bytes: 4-byte prefix 00000012, payload marker Barrier, version 00010006, 4-byte screen-name length 00000003, and UTF-8 bytes 6d3178.
Both captures also observed server-to-client QINF, CIAK, CROP and DSOP payload tokens, but this entry freezes no enter, leave, keyboard, mouse, clipboard, or keepalive semantics.

The claim is established by two captures where the only varied input is the deterministic synthetic screen name and the encoded length plus payload length vary accordingly.

sanitization.procedure: Allowlist sanitizer reconstructed TCP application payload frames from classic pcap. The committed fixture retains only the setup context and M1-031 control-message frames needed to freeze QINF, DINF, CIAK, CROP, DSOP, CALV, CNOP, CINN and COUT after approval. DCLP, DKDN and DKUP side-effect frame bodies are excluded and retained only as counts; after review, M1-031 may only skip their complete top-level frames by length without decoding or forwarding them. Packet headers, real addresses, ports, host names, user names and raw pcap bytes are not committed.

behaviors: The capture observed the Barrier server request screen info with QINF and the client answer with DINF carrying origin -1920,0, size 3648x1117, reserved 0 and cursor 772,594; this real display/cursor geometry is retained as low-sensitivity protocol evidence required by M1-031, not as host identity.
The capture observed setup control frames CIAK, CROP and DSOP with a zero DSOP value.
The capture observed bidirectional CALV keepalive and CNOP no-op frames.
The hotkey trigger produced a server-to-client CINN enter frame with x=772, y=594, sequence=1 and opaque modifier mask 0x2000, correlated with peer logs showing switch to the synthetic client screen.
The hotkey trigger produced a server-to-client COUT leave frame correlated with peer logs showing switch back to the Linux server screen.

wireClaims.assertion: For the observed external Barrier 2.4.0 control messages, QINF, CIAK, CROP, CALV, CNOP and COUT are 4-byte-token payloads with no body under the frozen 4-byte unsigned big-endian top-level length prefix.

The observed DINF frame body contains seven 16-bit big-endian fields: signed origin x, signed origin y, positive non-zero width, positive non-zero height, reserved zero, cursor x and cursor y. Cursor coordinate signedness is not established; M1-031 may accept only raw cursor values in 0x0000...0x7fff that also fall inside the current DINF rectangle and must fail closed otherwise.

The observed CINN frame body contains 16-bit big-endian x and y coordinate fields, a 4-byte big-endian observed sequence field, and an opaque 16-bit big-endian modifier mask; COUT has no body. Coordinate signedness and sequence increment semantics are not established; M1-031 may accept only raw enter coordinate values in 0x0000...0x7fff that also fall inside the current DINF rectangle and must fail closed otherwise.

The observed DSOP setup frame carries one 4-byte big-endian value observed as zero; no non-zero option semantics are established, and M1-031 must fail closed for non-zero values or any other DSOP payload length.

limitations: Only the M1-031 control-message contract is consumable by this entry after approval.
The capture used TLS disabled for observation only; production TLS defaults are unchanged and unvalidated by this entry.
DCLP clipboard and DKDN/DKUP hotkey side-effect frames were observed but removed from the committed fixture and are not consumable claims.

M1-031 may only skip the known excluded DCLP, DKDN and DKUP frames by top-level length without decoding their bodies or forwarding them to the KVM input pipeline; malformed excluded frames or unknown tokens remain fail-closed.
Diagnostics for skipped excluded frames may include only token, direction, count or length and non-sensitive reason metadata; they must not include frame body bytes, clipboard content or key data.

BARRIER-EVID-0004 remains append-only and still records that it did not establish enter, leave or keepalive semantics. This later pending entry is intended to resolve that specific M1-031 blocker after approval without rewriting BARRIER-EVID-0004.

The trigger attempted ctrl+F2, ctrl+F1, ctrl+F2, but the accepted capture contains only one CINN and one COUT transition. No repeated-enter or sequence increment behavior is claimed, and the DKDN/DKUP count asymmetry is treated as an excluded side effect.

A public PR history revision previously exposed one peer address in commands.json. The current committed command record is redacted; the historical exposure remains a review risk and is not consumable protocol evidence.
No Windows behavior is claimed.
Raw pcaps are not committed and this entry does not claim raw-pcap-to-sanitized re-derivation from the repository alone.

No clipboard content was present (both server clipboards were empty). The retained key frames encode exactly the synthetic xdotool sweep listed in the committed driver, which the reviewer confirmed marker by marker against the raw stream; no user input or user content was involved. The reviewer's byte scan found no printable run other than message codes, the marker word Barrier and the synthetic screen name capclient, and no address, host, user, path, certificate or probe bytes.

behaviors: 579 complete frames in capture order, 284 server-to-client and 295 client-to-server; every frame is a 4-byte unsigned big-endian length equal to the number of following bytes, then a 4-byte ASCII code.
Handshake frames 1-7 (hello, HelloBack for capclient, QINF, DINF 0,0,1600,900,0,800,450, CIAK, CROP, DSOP zero) match the layouts already approved in BARRIER-EVID-0004 and 0005.
The server sent CINN with sequence 1 at the first enter (frame 8) and sequence 3 at the second enter (frame 564), both at x=0 y=450 with mask 0x0000, and COUT with no body at frames 562 and 569.

Immediately after the first CINN the server sent two empty clipboard transfers, ids 0 and 1, sequence 0, each as start (ASCII 4), chunk (4 zero bytes: format count 0) and end, with one CALV interleaved inside each transfer (frames 9-16).
The client sent one CNOP for every server frame after DSOP (279 of 279) and answered every server CALV with a CALV (14 of 14); CALV and CNOP have no body.
Pointer, button, wheel, key, key-repeat frames were observed with the layouts and values stated in the wire claims; every DKDN had a matching DKUP with the same button and no key was left held.

Timing is not retained: from the raw stream the reviewer measured server CALV every 3.002-3.036 s after the enter burst, client CALV replies within 1.0 ms, client CNOP within 3.22 ms, and 14 DKRP frames 40 ms apart starting 661 ms after the held key went down; these are non-repeatable reviewer observations, not claims.

wireClaims.assertion: Server-to-client DMMV carries a 4-byte body read as two unsigned 16-bit big-endian fields, x then y, holding the absolute pointer position on the client in client pixels: the seven observed values (10,450), (10,460), (0,460), (0,450), (100,500), (101,501), (116,506) each equal the previous client position plus the driver's relative move from the enter point (0,450). Only values below 0x8000 were observed; signedness and clamping are not established.

Server-to-client DMDN and DMUP carry a 1-byte body holding a button number. For the driver's X button presses 1, 3, 2, 8, 9 the observed values were 1, 3, 2, 4, 5, each as a DMDN/DMUP pair with equal values, and a held button 1 produced DMDN, a DMMV, then DMUP. No other value was observed.

Server-to-client DMWM carries a 4-byte body read as two signed 16-bit big-endian fields, x delta then y delta. One wheel notch up, down, left and right produced bodies 0000 0078, 0000 ff88, ff88 0000 and 0078 0000, that is (0,+120), (0,-120), (-120,0), (+120,0). One notch per direction was observed; other magnitudes are not established.

Server-to-client DKDN and DKUP carry a 6-byte body of three unsigned 16-bit big-endian fields: key identifier, modifier mask, button. DKRP carries an 8-byte body of four such fields: key identifier, modifier mask, count, button; 14 DKRP frames with count 1 were observed between the DKDN and DKUP of a key held about 1.2 s. The button is the same in every down/up pair and in the repeats; the key identifier of an up may differ from its down (0x0041 down, 0x0061 up after Shift was released; likewise 0x0021/0x0031 and 0x005F/0x002D).

For this Linux server with the Xvfb default US keymap the key identifiers observed were: a-z 0x0061-0x007A, 0-9 0x0030-0x0039, space 0x0020, minus 0x002D, equal 0x003D, bracketleft 0x005B, bracketright 0x005D, backslash 0x005C, semicolon 0x003B, apostrophe 0x0027, grave 0x0060, comma 0x002C, period 0x002E, slash 0x002F, Return 0xEF0D, Escape 0xEF1B, Tab 0xEF09, BackSpace 0xEF08, Delete 0xEFFF, Insert 0xEF63, Left 0xEF51, Up 0xEF52, Right 0xEF53, Down 0xEF54, Home 0xEF50, End 0xEF57, Page Up 0xEF55, Page Down 0xEF56, keypad Enter 0xEF8D, F1-F12 0xEFBE-0xEFC9, volume up 0xE0AF, volume down 0xE0AE, mute 0xE0AD, Shift left/right 0xEFE1/0xEFE2, Control 0xEFE3/0xEFE4, Alt 0xEFE9/0xEFEA, Super 0xEFEB/0xEFEC, Caps Lock 0xEFE5; with Shift held, A 0x0041, exclam 0x0021, underscore 0x005F; with Caps Lock on, a 0x0041. The input-to-value pairing follows the committed driver order (frames 80-525) and was confirmed by the reviewer against the raw-stream markers. The button values are this server's X keycodes and are not a claim about any other server.

In the DKDN/DKUP/DKRP modifier mask, bit 0x0001 was set while Shift was held, 0x0002 while Control, 0x0004 while Alt, 0x0010 while Super and 0x1000 while Caps Lock was on, and 0x0003 while Control and Shift were held together. A modifier key's own DKDN carries the mask before it took effect and its DKUP carries the mask with its bit set (Shift down 0x0000, up 0x0001). For Caps Lock both the toggle-off DKDN and DKUP carried 0x1000, so a lock key's release does not reveal the resulting lock state. Bits other than these five were never set; their meaning is unknown.

CINN carries x, y as unsigned 16-bit big-endian, a 4-byte big-endian sequence and a 16-bit mask, as in BARRIER-EVID-0005; here the first enter carried sequence 1 and the second enter sequence 3, both x=0 y=450 mask 0x0000, with COUT (no body) between them. Sequence 2 was never on the wire; the increment rule is not established.

Server-to-client DCLP carries id (1 byte), sequence (4 bytes big-endian), mark (1 byte) and a 4-byte big-endian length followed by that many data bytes. On the first enter the server sent, for id 0 and then id 1, each with sequence 0: mark 1 with data ASCII 4, mark 2 with 4 data bytes 00000000, mark 3 with empty data; one CALV frame was interleaved inside each transfer. The mark-1 data is the decimal ASCII byte length of the mark-2 data; the mark-2 data read as a 4-byte big-endian format count was 0.
After DSOP the client sent exactly one CNOP (no body) per server frame, 279 for 279, and one CALV (no body) per server CALV, 14 for 14; COUT has no body in both observed instances.

limitations: One session of one external version pair on one host; the server was a Linux Barrier server on an Xvfb display with the default US keymap. No macOS Barrier server and no Windows peer were observed; the claim that frame layouts are server-platform independent is an inference and is not established here.

Button values in DKDN/DKUP/DKRP are this server's X keycodes; a consumer may rely only on their equality within a down/up pair and across plain and shifted presses of the same key, not on their values.
TLS was disabled for the observation only; nothing under TLS was observed and the product TLS default remains unvalidated by this entry.
No clamping of DMMV to the client screen was observed; the README's statement that positions are clamped is not supported.

Keepalive interval, reply latency and CNOP latency are reviewer measurements from the raw stream, which is not retained; they are not repeatable from the repository and are recorded here only as context.

Format 0's size equals the UTF-8 byte length of the probe set on the sending display (36 server, 37 client); format 1 was 54 bytes in both transfers despite the different probes, so its content is not a text-derived rendering of the probe; format 2 was 0 bytes in both. wireClaims.assertion: For the eleven US punctuation keys the server sent DKDN/DKUP with these key identifiers (plain, shifted) and buttons: minus 0x002D/0x005F 20; equal 0x003D/0x002B 21; bracketleft 0x005B/0x007B 34; bracketright 0x005D/0x007D 35; backslash 0x005C/0x007C 51; semicolon 0x003B/0x003A 47; apostrophe 0x0027/0x0022 48; grave 0x0060/0x007E 49; comma 0x002C/0x003C 59; period 0x002E/0x003E 60; slash 0x002F/0x003F 61. A shifted press is four frames: DKDN Shift 0xEFE1 mask 0 button 50; DKDN shifted id mask 0x0001; DKUP Shift mask 0x0001; DKUP plain id mask 0, same button as the down. Buttons are this server's X keycodes.

DCLP in both directions carries id (1 byte), a 4-byte big-endian sequence, mark (1 byte) and a 4-byte big-endian length followed by exactly that many data bytes. Marks were sent in the order 1, 2, 3 with no other frame of the transfer between them other than the server's interleaved CALV at enter; mark-1 data is the decimal ASCII byte length of the mark-2 data (118 for 118, 4 for 4, 119 for 119); mark-3 data is empty. The server's transfers carried sequence 0; the client's transfer carried sequence 1, the sequence of the CINN in force, as did its preceding CCLP.

The mark-2 data of a non-empty transfer is a 4-byte big-endian format count followed, per format, by a 4-byte big-endian format id, a 4-byte big-endian size and that many content bytes, with no trailing bytes: count 3 with ids 0, 1, 2 and sizes 36, 54, 0 (server to client) and 37, 54, 0 (client to server); an empty clipboard is count 0. Format 0's size equals the UTF-8 byte length of the probe on the sending display in both transfers. No format's meaning is established: content is zero-filled, and format 1's identical 54-byte size for two probes of different length shows it is not a rendering of the probe text.

After the client had sent CCLP and its DCLP transfer, the second CINN (sequence 3) was followed directly by COUT with no DCLP from the server. The same absence occurs in BARRIER-EVID-0006 where no client copy happened, so this observation does not discriminate clipboard ownership from a no-resend-on-re-enter rule.
